title: [FLINK-41063][runtime] Extract only sorting fields for large byte-key records

## What is the purpose of the change

Fix unnecessary payload serializer inference during DataStream large-record sorting. Both byte-key comparators currently extract the entire record as a sort key, although comparison only uses the byte-array key and timestamp. Consequently, `LargeRecordHandler` infers a serializer for the payload instead of using only the actual sorting fields. This can trigger unexpected Kryo usage or failures when generic types are disabled, despite a valid supplied record serializer.

## Brief change log
- Change `FixedLengthByteKeyComparator` and `VariableLengthByteKeyComparator` to extract the byte-array key and timestamp separately.
- Return matching flat comparators, preserving existing ordering.
- Add regression coverage for large-record spilling with a custom payload serializer and generic types disabled.

## Verifying this change

This change added tests and can be verified as follows:
-  Manually verified with an Apache Beam pipeline using the Flink Runner and `taskmanager.runtime.large-record-handler=true`. Without the fix, large-record spilling unexpectedly initialized Kryo for the Beam payload and failed with a classloader conflict, surfaced as “The sorter is closed already.” JFR revealed the underlying exception. The pipeline ran successfully with the patched build.
- `ByteKeyComparatorLargeRecordTest` covers both comparator variants, signed-byte and variable-length key ordering, timestamp tie-breaking, and payload round-tripping through large-record spilling.
